question: The Standard Deviation (SD) describes the variability of individual observations in a dataset, while the Standard Error (SE) describes the precision of the sample mean as an estimate of the population mean.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is actually true. SD measures spread of individual data points; SE measures precision of the mean estimate. Larger samples produce a smaller SE (more precise mean) but do not necessarily shrink the SD.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Exactly right. SD answers 'how spread out are the individual values?' — it is a property of the sample data. SE answers 'how reliable is our sample mean as an estimate of the true population mean?' — it decreases as sample size increases. Confusing the two is one of the most common errors in published medical literature.
